Case built for teaching: the underlying CT is real (public archive) and has no lesions; the lesions were added by computer with the noise of the original image. The realism is good but simplified: no histology, the outcome is the one set in the simulation.
Benign calcifications: diffuse homogeneous, central, laminated or "popcorn" (hamartoma). An eccentric or punctate calcification is not enough to say benign.
Fleischner 2017, single solid nodule (adults ≥ 35 years, non-oncologic, outside screening): < 6 mm no routine follow-up (high risk: optional CT at 12 months); 6-8 mm CT at 6-12 months; > 8 mm CT at 3 months, PET-CT or sampling. The measurement is the mean of the long and short axis, in lung window, rounded to the millimeter.
Ogni nodulo va guardato in finestra medi: Every nodule must be looked at in the mediastinal window: complete calcification = benign; solid > 8 mm = CT at 3 months, PET or biopsy.
